source.title: Beyond Single-Model Views for Deep Learning: Optimization versus Generalizability of Stochastic Optimization Algorithms
source.authors: Toki Tahmid Inan; Mingrui Liu; A. Shehu

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to be the full paper. Some table formatting and algorithm abbreviations are garbled, but the relevant Table 4 entries are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Compares low-loss model populations with high-test-performance populations using test-set metrics and statistical tests, a different method bearing on the relationship between training loss and generalization. It does not test the specific interventions in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on whether low-loss models have different test performance from models selected for high test performance. Those population comparisons bear on the claim's generalization subject but do not measure any listed version's specified behavior. Cited prior findings and synthetic-landscape results are not included as rows. Table 4 reports medians and standard deviations; the paper's prose also reports tests of SetA versus SetB, but those comparisons do not measure a listed version.
record.test_reason: The study compares loss-selected and test-performance-selected model populations and benchmarks stochastic optimizers. None of its own results measures V1–V8. SAM performance is not a measurement of magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gap; the optimizer comparisons do not include adaptive methods.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' interpretation: population-based benchmarking suggests generally comparable performance for loss-selected and test-performance-selected models and for the tested optimizers. The authors additionally emphasize that SGD and BH variants match SAM with half the gradient evaluations. Their blanket interpretation needs qualification: Table 6 includes significant comparisons for SGD versus SAM on GoEmotions (p=0.035478) and SAM versus NiM-BH on CIFAR-100 (p=0.0458), contrary to the accompanying assertion that every p-value exceeds 0.05.
record.recipe_differences: Population-based analysis of optimizer trajectories and test metrics; it does not use the original interventions or measurements in the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on task and optimizer; the paper notes exceptions to the generally non-significant SetA versus SetB performance comparisons, including NiM-SGD and NiG-BH on GoEmotions-BERT.

fits_no_version.finding: Most reported tests do not reject a difference between loss-selected and test-performance-selected populations. Some comparisons are significant, with exceptions depending on task, optimizer, tuning, and statistical test. Non-rejection does not establish equivalence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Across the tested trajectories, selecting low-loss checkpoints often yields test-performance distributions that the reported tests do not distinguish from those selected directly for test performance.

record.problems: The real-world comparison uses five random restarts and 50 models per optimizer. The authors state that hyperparameter optimization was attempted but was computationally costly. Table 4 reports medians and standard deviations, while the authors' distribution comparisons use p-values; these results do not directly report train-test gaps. The supplied text has apparent formatting/typographical inconsistencies in some tables and descriptions.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. Table 2 and Table 3 SetA-versus-SetB p-values are additional statistical comparisons of the same population-performance question and are not separately cataloged because no listed version is tested and Table 4 already records the reported performance summaries.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out performance under the same training recipe.
Width-dependent test error beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and compensating recipe changes.
Dropout interventions, training-set size dependence, and interaction with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps at similar training loss, and comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Table 4's caption describes medians and median standard deviations, whereas the prose describes averages and standard deviations; retain that inconsistency. Flattened table ordering prevents confident repair of several population assignments. All rows remain unrelated to V1–V8 regardless of those repairs. No additional result bearing on a listed version was found in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training, natural-label comparison against chance, or test error after fitting random labels.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold comparison.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
No adaptive optimizer comparison, learning-rate-only tuning comparison, or Adam/SGD comparison.
No batch-size comparison or fixed-epoch large-batch penalty.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or norm/margin measure.
